chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Darraj, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).
Regarding the man who performs ritual bath (ghusl) for Ihram, then wipes his head with a handkerchief; he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram, the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does wiping the head with a cloth during the Ihram bath invalidate the ritual?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies a specific detail in the ritual purification (ghusl) for Ihram, affirming that wiping the head with a cloth (mandil) does not invalidate the state of consecration. In Shia fiqh, this ruling is significant as it distinguishes between the essential acts of ghusl and incidental actions, ensuring the pilgrim's ritual purity remains intact for entering the sacred state. The chain of transmission highlights the continuity of Imami scholarly tradition regarding the practicalities of Hajj rituals.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)
regarding the man who washes for the Ihraam, then he wipes his head with a towel. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from ibn Darraj who has said the following: “About a man who takes Ghusl (bath), then wipes his head with a towel, one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
